programme.title: The Carol Burnett Show - S11:E21 - Steve Martin/Betty White

programme.title: The Carol Burnett Show - S1:E4 - Tim Conway, Lucille Ball
programme.desc: Highlights include: two women (Carol and guest Lucille Ball) go to the "Café Argentine" whose staff includes a goose-stepping maitre d' (Harvey); Carol as a housewife fighting off a recalcitrant washing machine and attacking pigeons, only to end up impaled by a medieval lance; "Carol and Sis" sing a rendition of "I Dig Rock and Roll Music"; guest Tim Conway plays a bumbling TV news anchor; two rent-a-car employees (Carol, Lucy) vie for the attentions of a traveler (Tim); guest Gloria Loring performs "Goin' Out of My Head" and "Try to Remember"; a woman (Carol) experiences the downside of marrying a superhero (Harvey); and Carol and Lucy sing and dance to a barroom medley.

programme.title: The Carol Burnett Show - S1:E9 - Richard Chamberlain and Gloria Loring

programme.title: Relative Justice with Judge Rhonda Wills
programme.desc: Amina Henderson walks into small claims court carrying invoices, receipts, photographs, and documentation of lost wages. She is suing her cousin, Lyric O’Neal, for $1,400, claiming unpaid services she provided, damage caused to her property, and wages she lost due to Lyric’s actions. Lyric defends himself, insisting: “I don’t owe that much. I didn’t cause all of this, and some of it was voluntary.”

programme.title: Relative Justice with Judge Rhonda Wills
programme.desc: Eleazar Rodriguez walks into small claims court carrying a signed loan agreement, bank transfer records, and communications with his cousin, Nashawn Graves. He is suing for $5,000, claiming that Nashawn borrowed the money and has not repaid it despite repeated requests. Nashawn defends himself, insisting: “I don’t owe that money. That was a gift, not a loan.”

programme.title: Relative Justice with Judge Rhonda Wills
programme.desc: Jamar Pinkett walks into small claims court holding receipts, photographs, and repair/replacement estimates for three iPhones allegedly smashed by his girlfriend, Deida Rodriguez. He is suing for $1,736, claiming that Deida intentionally or negligently damaged his property. Deida defends herself, insisting: “I didn’t do it on purpose. I shouldn’t have to pay for accidents.”

programme.title: Relative Justice with Judge Rhonda Wills
programme.desc: Jim Coyle walks into small claims court carrying a signed contract, text messages, and receipts for preparations for a DJ party he was hired to perform at. He is suing his brother-in-law, Donavan Lunar, for $1,200, claiming that Donavan breached the agreement by canceling the event without paying the agreed fee.

programme.title: Relative Justice with Judge Rhonda Wills
programme.desc: Corta Ishman walks into small claims court carrying lease agreements, payment records, and messages documenting the shared living arrangement with her cousin, Latoyia Brown. She is suing for $3,000, representing several months of unpaid rent that Latoyia agreed to pay while sharing the residence. Latoyia defends herself, insisting: “I don’t owe that much. We shared the place, and I shouldn’t have to pay the full amount.”
